statement.summary: Lemma 3.1 is frozen as two Props: part (i) is `fixCountStatement` (Lagrange divisibility made explicit, then the count), part (ii) is `fixJoinStatement` (an equality of sets of configurations, for a family indexed by `Fin ℓ`). `fixLemmaStatement` is their conjunction.
deltas: N/|H| is ℕ-division; its exactness (|H| divides n^d) is an explicit extra conjunct, so no truncation can hide.
Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1 from Definition 2.1; (i) allows σ ≥ 1 (counting statement), (ii) keeps σ ≥ 2.
The family H_1,…,H_ℓ is `H : Fin ℓ → AddSubgroup (Lat n d)`; ℓ = 0 is allowed (a true extension).

maps.label: a subgroup H ≤ 𝒜
maps.note: 𝒜 = ℤ_n^d is `Lat n d := Fin d → ZMod n`; a subgroup of the additive group is an `AddSubgroup`.

maps.label: finite family H_1,…,H_ℓ

lean.text: (ℓ : ℕ) (H : Fin ℓ → AddSubgroup (Lat n d))

maps.note: A finite family is a function from `Fin ℓ`; ℓ = 0 (empty family) is included.

lean.text: Nat.card (fixedBy (Fin σ) H) = σ ^ (n ^ d / Nat.card H)

maps.label: |Fix(H)|

lean.text: {s | ∀ h ∈ H, shift h s = s}

maps.note: Fix(H) = configurations fixed by every element of H (`fixedBy`, Definitions.lean); |·| = `Nat.card`.

maps.label: σ^{|𝒜|/|H|}
maps.note: |𝒜| = N = n^d written out; `/` is ℕ-division, exact by the divisibility conjunct.

maps.label: |H| divides N (Lagrange)
maps.note: Implicit in the paper (the exponent must be an integer); made explicit so the ℕ-division cannot truncate.

maps.label: standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1
maps.note: From Definition 2.1; counting statements allow σ = 1.

lean.text:
(⋂ a, fixedBy (Fin σ) (H a))
        = fixedBy (Fin σ) (AddSubgroup.closure (⋃ a, (H a : Set (Lat n d))))

maps.label: ⋂_{a=1}^ℓ Fix(H_a)
maps.note: Indexed intersection over a : Fin ℓ.

maps.label: ⟨H_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ H_ℓ⟩

lean.text: AddSubgroup.closure (⋃ a, (H a : Set (Lat n d)))

maps.note: The generated subgroup is literally the closure of the union of carriers.

maps.label: σ ≥ 2 kept in (ii)
maps.note: Not a counting statement, so the standing σ ≥ 2 is kept; the identity holds for every alphabet.
